lines.say: Atari once buried truckloads of video games in the New Mexico desert.
The most famous one was E.T., for the Atari 2600.
lines.cap: The most famous one was E.T., for the Atari 2600.

lines.say: Its programmer, Howard Scott Warshaw, had only five weeks to make the whole game.
Atari made five million cartridges, but only about one and a half million sold at first.
lines.cap: Atari made 5 million cartridges, but only about 1.5 million sold at first.

lines.say: Then in September 1983, trucks dumped Atari games at a landfill in Alamogordo, and covered them in concrete.
For years, people called it an urban legend.

args.text: MILLIONS OF E.T. GAMES UNDER THE DESERT?

lines.say: In April 2014, a film crew dug it up, in front of a crowd.
They found about 1,300 cartridges, from 59 different games. Not millions of E.T.s.
Atari's own records said about 700,000 cartridges were buried in total.
lines.cap: Atari's own records said about 700,000 cartridges were buried in total.

lines.say: The city sold them online, and one E.T. cartridge went for over fifteen hundred dollars. Another went to the Smithsonian.
lines.cap: The city sold them online, and one E.T. cartridge went for over $1,500. Another went to the Smithsonian.
